config.frame: six families named in the design's gate zero plus one kill candidate slot, fixed before any date was read

criteria.detail: 7 cells in the frame, 7 reported, 1 with a date that cannot be pinned and reported anyway (England); 0 cells where the hand-written sign disagrees with the computed one
criteria.name: B33-12 the polity frame was fixed before any date was read, and every cell in it is reported including the ones whose dates cannot be pinned

criteria.detail: after 6, same_act 0, before 0, undated 1; gaps in years for the signed cells: Roman Republic 128 to 172, Qin and Han 19 to 172, France 256 to 256, Uganda Protectorate 45 to 54, Great Britain 103 to 107, Athens 7 to 80
criteria.name: B33-13 the sign: no polity's graduated per-person tax arrives before a qualifying register

after.reads: the tax arrives after the register

before.reads: the tax arrives before any qualifying register

same_act.reads: one reform creates the list and the classes together, so there is no order to read; this is the tightest form of the dependence and the weakest reading of the sequence

undated.reads: one of the two dates cannot be pinned, so no verdict

criteria.detail: matched 3, extended 1, overrun_then_extended 1, overrun 1, counterexample 0, unknown 1; cells not in the fitting state: England 7 classes, overrun, ran: no; France 22 classes, extended, ran: yes; Uganda Protectorate 2 classes, unknown, ran: yes; Athens 3 classes, overrun_then_extended, ran: yes
criteria.name: B33-14 where the class count exceeds what the prior list can tell apart, either the list was extended or the tax did not run; no cell has both an overrun and a tax that ran

counterexample.reads: the class count exceeds it, no roll was built, and the tax ran anyway

extended.reads: the class count exceeds it and the state built the missing roll, and the tax ran

matched.reads: the class count fits what the prior list can tell apart

overrun.reads: the class count exceeds it, no roll was built, and the tax did not run

overrun_then_extended.reads: the class count exceeds it, the tax leaked for a while, and the state then built the missing roll; added when a cell landed between overrun and extended rather than on either

unknown.reads: the list's resolution cannot be pinned, so no verdict

criteria.detail: axis carried: no 2, partial 1, unknown 1, yes 3; misaligned cells, meaning the axis is carried and the count still did not fit or the axis is not carried and it did: none; cells left out because one side is unknown: Uganda Protectorate
criteria.name: B33-17 the sign test asks whether the register can find the person, not whether it can tell the classes apart; those are two questions and this one names the cells where the answer differs

criteria.name: B33-15 control: a levy keyed to an object or to a place is not a per-person graduated tax and must not be counted as one

cells.register: the deme citizen-lists; enrolment in one becomes the requirement for citizenship
cells.register_note: this cell was left unresolved on the first run and is resolved here by one narrow question: was Solon's wealth census a maintained list. It was not. Centuries later the class was still established by asking the man at the moment he needed it, and the answer was not checked against anything, which is what the tightened definition excludes. So the register for this cell is not Solon's census of 594 but the deme lists of Cleisthenes. The tightened definition was fixed before this cell was looked at, and it costs the reading that would have been most convenient here
cells.resolution_note: the deme list carries citizenship and deme, not property, while the eisphora's bands are cut on property; the gap was filled by declaration and the wealthy concealed part of their estates, and in 378/7 the basis founded on the Solonian classes was abolished and scales of value for all taxed persons were introduced, which is the missing roll being built
cells.tax: the eisphora, the direct levy on citizens, whose bands were founded on the Solonian classes; the three wealthiest classes paid one talent, half a talent and one sixth of a talent
